title: A tank with a hole
prompt:
A tap fills an empty tank in 12 hours. The tank has a hole in the bottom, and with the hole open the same tap takes 18 hours to fill the empty tank. The water leaks out at a steady rate whatever the depth.

If the tank were full, with the tap off, how many hours would the hole take to empty it?
hints: What fraction of the tank does the tap fill in one hour with no leak, and what fraction does it gain in one hour with the leak?
Where did the difference between those two fractions go?
If that fraction of a full tank leaks away each hour, how long does the whole tank take to empty?
solution:
**36 hours.**

Think in fractions of the tank per hour. The tap fills 1/12 of the tank each hour. With the leak open, the tank gains only 1/18 each hour, so the leak removes the difference: 1/12 − 1/18 = 1/36 of the tank per hour.

If 1/36 of a full tank leaks away each hour, the leak alone takes **36** hours to empty it.

The common slip is subtracting the times, 18 − 12 = 6. Times do not subtract, but rates do.
